question:
In the given figure, ∠POQ = 100°, ∠POR = 80°. Then, ∠PSQ = ?(O is the center of the circle)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/839c656315e3d27efe699de47af203a61a9eceda1dc62f94e2b6cfeb1fec346a.png]
solution:
**Given:**

In figure 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/839c656315e3d27efe699de47af203a61a9eceda1dc62f94e2b6cfeb1fec346a.png] 

∠POQ = 100°, ∠POR = 80°

**Concept Used:**

If the base of triangles is the same, then the angle made by the base in every triangle is equal.

The diameter of a triangle make right-angle at any point on the circle.

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/839c656315e3d27efe699de47af203a61a9eceda1dc62f94e2b6cfeb1fec346a.png] 

As, ∠POQ = 100°, ∠POR = 80°

Now, In ΔPOQ,

As, PO and QO are the radius of circle.

⇒ ∠OPQ = ∠OQP

⇒ ∠OPQ + ∠OQP + ∠POQ = 180°

⇒ ∠OQP + ∠OQP = 180° - 100° = 80° 

⇒ ∠OQP = 80°/2 = 40° 

Now, in ΔPRQ, 

∠PRQ = 180° - (∠RPQ + ∠RQP) = 180° - (90° + 40°) = 50° [RQ is diameter and ∠RPQ is made by it]

Now, The base of both the triangles RPQ and PSQ is the same, i.e., PQ

⇒ ∠PRQ = ∠PSQ 

⇒ ∠PSQ = 50° 

**∴ The measure of ∠PSQ is 50°.**
